comment:
The evaluation began with checking the Norminette and running external testers (including Tripouille). Everything passed successfully.
We then moved to the explanation phase. I asked the evaluee to explain the difference between `memcpy` and `memmove`. He was unable to explain it using his own code and repeatedly gave the same answer, which did not address how the function actually works. He also could not explain the forward and backward copy conditions or mention the importance of overlapping memory regions.
Next, I asked the evaluee to write a simple `main` function demonstrating `memmove`. He struggled to understand the function's parameters, searched online for the function definition, and even looked up basic C array syntax. He was also unable to declare a `char *` pointer correctly. At that point, the evaluee asked me to explain the concept myself. I spent approximately one hour explaining how `memmove` works in the hope that he would understand it. Afterward, he finally grasped the concept but claimed that this had been their original explanation, which was not accurate.
Since both the explanation and live coding parts were unsuccessful, I continued with questions about the `split` function, specifically memory allocation, deallocation, and the purpose of the `free_all` helper in preventing memory leaks. Once again, the evaluee was unable to explain the implementation they had written.
Throughout the evaluation, the evaluee became increasingly aggressive. When I informed them that I could not pass the project, he insisted that I had no right to fail them and said they wanted another evaluator to prove I was wrong. I asked him to allow me to complete the evaluation, but he repeatedly interrupted me and would not let me finish. maintain a positive learning environment:

1. **Maintain Respect and Constructiveness**
- Be polite, courteous and respectful during the 
  evaluation process. The well-being of the community depends on it.
- Constructive feedback helps your peers improve. The well-being of 
  the community depends on a supportive approach.

2. **Identify and Discuss Issues**
- Work with the student or group to identify potential issues in their project.
  Take the time to discuss and debate any problems you find.

3. **Acknowledge Different Approaches**
- Recognize that different students may have different interpretations of the
  project’s instructions and requirements.
- Keep an open mind and grade as honestly and fairly as possible.
- The effectiveness of peer evaluation depends on serious and thoughtful assessment.

4. **Handling Incorrect Exercises**
- If you encounter an incorrect exercise, stop the assessment immediately.
- Do not proceed to the next exercise if a previous one is incorrect.
- Use the appropriate flags to report the issue and provide feedback to the student.
scale.guidelines_md:
- Only grade the work that was turned in the Git repository of the evaluated 
  student or group.

- Double-check that the Git repository belongs to the student(s). Ensure that 
  the project is the one expected. Also, check that 'git clone' is used in an 
  empty folder.

- Check carefully that no malicious aliases were used to fool you and make you 
  evaluate something that is not the content of the official repository.

- To avoid any surprises and if applicable, review together any scripts used 
  to facilitate the grading (scripts for testing or automation).

- Do not blindly trust any scripts. The tester could be wrong!

- Check the makefile: no wildcard, no relink, or the final grade is 0.

- Use make, then make --debug to be sure.

- If you have not completed the assignment you are going to evaluate, you have 
  to read the entire subject prior to starting the evaluation process.

- Use the available flags to report an empty repository, a non-functioning 
  program, a Norm error, cheating, and so forth. 
  In these cases, the evaluation process ends and the final grade is 0, 
  or -42 in case of cheating. However, except for cheating, students are 
  strongly encouraged to review together the work that was turned in, in order 
  to identify any mistakes that shouldn't be repeated in the future.

- You should never have to edit any file except the configuration file if it 
  exists. If you want to edit a file, take the time to explicit the reasons 
  with the evaluated student and make sure both of you are okay with this.

- You must also verify the absence of memory leaks. Any memory allocated on 
  the heap must be properly freed before the end of execution. 
  You are allowed to use any of the different tools available on the computer, 
  such as leaks, valgrind, or e_fence. In case of memory leaks, tick the 
  appropriate flag.

comment: Amazing project delivered by the trans-and-dance team. The idea for the project is original, based on a quiz game show 1 z 10, and it was selected in a rigorous process in the early stages of working on the project. The team showed a good team spirit during the evaluation, it was a pleasure to listen to them explain what they did, why they did it, and also about how they were updating their decisions on the go according to the needs. Just filling out an evaluation sheet is one thing but that's not what the Pedago in 42Warsaw does. The time and effort Alina put into reviewing our project is incredible. Extra thanks for the the Pedago Manager, going far and beyond to support us through our highs and lows. It would have been so much harder without him.
	
A haiku for Luke,
I'm sure he will love this one.
Cross us off your list.

comment: Well done project! A small modification was required in the function scheduling start of the threads. I also think the project should be more explicit about the order in which each thread should be started, because depending on the system's scheduler to order which philosopher will grab the fork first is not reliable and can cause philosopher to die even though the program works in a way described in the subject. One fix would be to make philosophers with even id start first but I suppose it would be communication between philosophers. I don't feel it should fail the project as you understand the problem well and did a conscious decision to not do that. Good work nevertheless!
feedback: Very good evaluator checked my code thoroughly and in ways I didn’t even know and overall very nice guy

scale.guidelines_md:
- Only grade the work that was turned in the Git repository of the evaluated 
  student or group.

- Double-check that the Git repository belongs to the student(s). Ensure that 
  the project is the one expected. Also, check that 'git clone' is used in an 
  empty folder.

- Check carefully that no malicious aliases were used to fool you and make you 
  evaluate something that is not the content of the official repository.

- To avoid any surprises and if applicable, review together any scripts used 
  to facilitate the grading (scripts for testing or automation).

- If you have not completed the assignment you are going to evaluate, you have 
  to read the entire subject prior to starting the evaluation process.

- Use the available flags to report an empty repository, a non-functioning 
  program, a Norm error, cheating, and so forth. 
  In these cases, the evaluation process ends and the final grade is 0, 
  or -42 in case of cheating. However, except for cheating, students are 
  strongly encouraged to review together the work that was turned in, in order 
  to identify any mistakes that shouldn't be repeated in the future.

- Remember that for the duration of the defense, no segfault,no premature or 
  uncontrolled termination of the program; otherwise, the final grade is 0.
  Use the appropriate flag. 
  You should never have to edit any file except the configuration file if it 
  exists. If you want to edit a file, take the time to explicit the reasons 
  with the evaluated student and make sure both of you are okay with this.

- You must verify the absence of data races. 
  You are allowed to use any of the available tools on the computer, such as 
  Valgrind with '--tool=helgrind' and '--tool=drd'.  In case of any 
  data-race, the evaluation stops here.

- You must also verify the absence of memory leaks. Any memory allocated on 
  the heap must be properly freed before the end of execution. You are 
  allowed to use any of the different tools available on the computer, such 
  as leaks, valgrind, or e_fence. In case of memory leaks, tick the 
  appropriate flag.
